15354140_d319cccf.text: The data demonstrate that GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons directly synapse onto GluR cells and suggest a low number of neuronal release sites.

15354140_021d66ce.text: GluR cells: These are unique glutamate receptor-expressing cells that escape classification as neurons, astrocytes, or oligodendrocytes (Jabs et al., 2005). GluR cells co-express S100β (astrocyte marker), NG2, and neuronal genes, and receive direct synaptic input from both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.

15354140_afe52706.text: These cells show characteristic nodules along their processes and represent a distinct population that bridges glial and neuronal properties (Jabs et al., 2005).

15354140_c1bc8ebc.text: Sub-threshold stimulation to Schaffer collaterals resulted in stimulus-correlated, postsynaptic responses in a subpopulation of EGFP-positive cells studied with the patch-clamp technique in acute slices

15354140_d16f4fee.text: these cells are characterized by an extended net of thin processes surrounding the soma as revealed through intracellular labelling ( Fig. 2A 1 left). The processes characteristically displayed small nodules and covered an area of 3445±2010 m 2 (n=6). All GluR cells tested expressed the proteoglycan, NG2 (6/6 cells; Fig. 2A 1 right). As in adult mice (Wallraff et al., 2004), these cells never displayed dye coupling and did not contact blood vessels.
